title: Realizing a prescribed fibre-regular germ as a smooth Cartier cut
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $x_s\in X_s$ denote the point over $x$ in the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Write $R=\mathcal O_{X_s,x_s}$, and let $h\in\mathfrak m_x\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be a specified germ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk, def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose its image $\bar h\in R$ is a nonzerodivisor, meaning that multiplication by $\bar h$ is injective, and that the image of $dh$ in $\Omega^1_{X/S,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)$ is nonzero [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X$ of $x$ there exist an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}H\subseteq W$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $a\in H$ with germ $a_x=h$ such that $D=\operatorname{Spec}(H/(a))\hookrightarrow U$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-trf-effective-cartier-center], contains $x$, and $D\to S$ is smooth. If $x_D\in D$ is the unique point mapping to $x$, then the canonical local-ring map induces
$$R/(\bar h)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{D_s,(x_D)_s},\qquad [c/u]\longmapsto [(c\bmod a_s)/(u\bmod a_s)],$$
where the formula is read on any affine fibre chart through $x_s$, $a_s$ is the fibre equation, and denominators avoid the prime of $x_s$. This isomorphism induces the identity on the common residue field $\kappa(x)$. The fibre closed immersion $D_s\hookrightarrow U_s$ is also an effective Cartier divisor. No Noetherian condition on $X$ or $S$, no closed-point condition on $x_s$, and no separability hypothesis are imposed.

source.place: Tag 057C, lemma-slice-smooth-given-element: affine realization of the given germ with smooth Cartier zero scheme; its proof uses the fibre quotient local ring. The explicit fibre-regular hypothesis is available from the preceding germ lemma.

external.place: Tag 062Y, lemma-fibre-Cartier (3), locally principal case; relative effective Cartier divisors have effective Cartier fibres (lemma-relative-Cartier).

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] supplies affine neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $s$ and $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ of $x$, with $f(U_0)\subset V$ and $B_0$ finitely presented over $A$. Let $Q_0$ be the prime of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], write the specified $h$ as $r/t\in (B_0)_{Q_0}$ with $t\notin Q_0$. The basic-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] gives $e\notin Q_0$ with $D(e)\subset U_0\cap W$. Replace $U_0$ by $D(et)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=(B_0)_{et}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]; both $e$ and $t$ are units, so $a=r/t\in B$ has germ exactly $h$. This algebra is still finitely presented: adjoining one variable $T$ and the relation $(et)T-1$ to a finite presentation of $B_0$ presents $B$. The flat affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $B$ flat over $A$. Write $Q\subset B$ for $x$.

source.place: Tag 057C, lemma-slice-smooth-given-element, initial affine shrinking; Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, initial germ representation

proof.text: Put $F=B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], the fibre of the chosen open is open in $X_s$ through $x_s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $(\operatorname{Spec}B)_s=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $R=F_P$ for the prime $P$ of $x_s$, whose contraction is $Q$. The image of $a$ in $F_P$ is $\bar h$. Since $h\in\mathfrak m_x$, its image lies in the maximal ideal of $F_P$; hence $F_P/(\bar h)\ne0$. Together with the assumed injective multiplication, this says the singleton list $(a)$ is regular in $F_P$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Apply [lem-pur-fiber-regular-sequence-neighbourhood] to the flat finitely presented $A$-algebra $B$ and this singleton. It gives $g\notin Q$ such that $a$ is a nonzerodivisor in $B_g$. Set $U_1=D(g)$ and $D_1=\operatorname{Spec}(B_g/(a))$. These are the affine open and closed subscheme of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By [def-trf-effective-cartier-center], $D_1$ is effective Cartier in $U_1$. As $a\in Q$, it contains the unique point over $x$.

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, proof of (1), singleton case via Tag 062Y(3)

proof.text: The restricted ambient map $U_1\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. View $a$ as a section of the trivial invertible module $\mathcal O_{U_1}$. Its zero scheme is $D_1$ by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties]. The compatibility under restriction in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] identifies its residue differential at $x$ with the specified $dh(x)$, which is nonzero. Apply [lem-zl-hypersurface-nonzero-relative-differential]: there is an open $O\subset D_1$ containing $x$ on which $D_1\to S$ is smooth. The closed immersion identifies $D_1$ with its subspace in $U_1$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], so choose an ambient open $N\subset U_1$ with $O=D_1\cap N$. Choose a basic affine open $U=D(v)\ni x$ inside $N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Write $H=(B_g)_v$, and still denote the image of $a$ by $a$. Then $U\subset W$, $a_x=h$, and $D=\operatorname{Spec}(H/(a))$ is an open subscheme of $O$, hence smooth over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Localization preserves the injection given by multiplication by $a$, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]; thus $D\hookrightarrow U$ remains effective Cartier and contains $x$.

source.place: Tag 057C, lemma-slice-smooth-given-element, nonzero differential and final shrinking; the differential implication is supplied by the existing hypersurface criterion

proof.text: All the final schemes lie over $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The smooth restriction lemma gives $D\to V$ smooth, so [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] give $H/(a)$ flat over $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to the exact sequence $0\to H\xrightarrow{a}H\to H/(a)\to0$ and the $A$-module $\kappa(s)$. It shows that multiplication by $a_s$ is injective on $C=H\otimes_A\kappa(s)$. The affine fibre-product formula and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], applied to $H\to C$ and $(a)\subset H$, identify $U_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $D_s=\operatorname{Spec}(C/(a_s))$ with their natural closed immersion. Thus [def-trf-effective-cartier-center] proves that $D_s\hookrightarrow U_s$ is effective Cartier. The flatness of $H/(a)$ is what permits this base change of the injection.

source.place: Tag 056Q, lemma-relative-Cartier, proof by tensoring the principal exact sequence

proof.text:
Let $P\subset C$ be the prime of $x_s$, and $\widetilde P=P/(a_s)$ the corresponding prime of $C/(a_s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $U_s$ is open in $X_s$ through $x_s$, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $R=C_P$, with $\bar h=a_s/1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] to $C$, $I=(a_s)$ and $\widetilde P$. Its stated fraction formula gives the canonical isomorphism
$$R/(\bar h)=C_P/(a_s)C_P\xrightarrow{\sim}(C/(a_s))_{\widetilde P}=\mathcal O_{D_s,(x_D)_s},\qquad[c/u]\longmapsto[(c\bmod a_s)/(u\bmod a_s)].$$
The last equality is again the affine stalk identification. These maps are induced by the actual fibre closed immersion of the preceding step. On any other affine fibre chart the same localization-of-quotient statement applies to its equation and prime; the map is still induced by that closed immersion, so this proves the asserted chart-independent formula. The prime correspondence for the surjection $H\to H/(a)$ in [def-weil-closed-immersion] also identifies $x_D$ uniquely.

source.place: Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient, fraction formula; Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, stalks

proof.text: Finally, for a local ring $L$ and ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_L$, the residue field of $L/I$ is $(L/I)/(\mathfrak m_L/I)=L/\mathfrak m_L$: the induced map sends the class of $b$ to the same class of $b$. Apply this first to $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and the base maximal ideal (using [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient]), and then to $R$ and $(\bar h)$. Apply the same fibre-stalk statement to $D\to S$, and the closed-immersion affine local quotient description from Step 5 to $D\hookrightarrow U$. Under all these identifications the residue fields are $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The fraction isomorphism of Step 5 sends the residue of $c/u$ to the residue of the same fraction, so its residue-field map is the identity. No step used a closed-point, Noetherian-base or separability hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem exists_prescribed_germ_smooth_cartier_cut {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] (x : X) (h : X.presheaf.stalk x) (hh : h ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (hregular : Function.Injective (fun z : (f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x) ↦ (f.fiberStalkMap x).hom h * z)) (hdiff : ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hxV : x ∈ V) (b : Γ(X, V)), X.presheaf.germ V x hxV b = h ∧ f.relativeDifferentialValue V x hxV b) (W : X.Opens) (hxW : x ∈ W) : ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hxU : x ∈ U) (a : Γ(X, U)), U ≤ W ∧ X.presheaf.germ U x hxU a = h ∧ IsEffectiveCartierCenter (prescribedGermCutι a) ∧ Smooth (prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec ≫ f) ∧ (∃! xD : prescribedGermCut a, (prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) xD = x) ∧ IsEffectiveCartierCenter (prescribedGermFiberMap (hU.fromSpec ≫ f) (prescribedGermCutι a) (f x)) ∧ ∃ (y : ((prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) ≫ f).fiber (f x)) (hy : prescribedGermFiberMap f (prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) (f x) y = f.asFiber x) (e : ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x) ⧸ Ideal.span {(f.fiberStalkMap x).hom h}) ≃+* (((prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) ≫ f).fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk y), (∀ c : (f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x), e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ c) = prescribedGermStalkMap (prescribedGermFiberMap f (prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) (f x)) (f.asFiber x) y hy c) ∧ ∃ r : (((prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) ≫ f).fiber (f x)).residueField y ≃+* X.residueField x, ∀ b : X.presheaf.stalk x, r (((((prescribedGermCutι a ≫ hU.fromSpec) ≫ f).fiber (f x)).residue y) (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ ((f.fiberStalkMap x).hom b)))) = X.residue x b
lean.note: Canonical principal quotient, fibre pullback map and point-transported stalk map are constructed as helpers. Nonzero differential is expressed using a representative of the prescribed germ and the existing relativeDifferentialValue; the existing helper definitions are owned by def-trf-fibre-stalk-map and def-trf-relative-differential-value in stmt_deps; the accompanying theorem nodes remain in proof_deps.
